 OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED  24.10.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.171/2014 ON THE FILE OF THE  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:45372  MFA No. 2145 of 2017 PRINCIPAL DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE & MACT,
CHAMARAJANAGAR, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant for seeking enhancement of compensation as well as modification of liability fastened on respondent No.1/owner.
2. The factum of accident and injuries sustained by the appellant/claimant are not in dispute.
Respondent No.2/Insurance Company is disputing the liability on the ground that the offending vehicle (Auto Rickshaw) was not having permit as on the date of the accident.
3. For the sake of convenience and easy reference, the parties are referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded global compensation of Rs.31,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
fixing the liability on respondent No.1/owner by exonerating respondent No.2/Insurance Company on the reason that as on the date of accident i.e., on 01.04.2014, the offending vehicle (Auto Rickshaw) was not having permit
, on this reason liability is ordered on respondent No.1/owner of the Auto Rickshaw.
5. From the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the appellant/claimant has suffered fracture of right metatarsal bone.

6. The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:
Sl. Particulars Amount in Rs.
No.
1. Towards injury, pain and suffering 20,000/-
2. Towards medical expenses 2,000/-

7.
The Doctor is not examined to prove as to what is his percentage of disability.
Considering the nature of injuries NC: 2024:KHC:45372 sustained, compensation of Rs.31,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is on lesser side.
Under the heads 'incidental expenses', 'loss of income during treatment period' and 'loss of amenities', the appellant/claimant is entitled for higher amount of compensation.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries sustained the Court is of the opinion to make additional global compensation of Rs.35,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The said amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. REGARDING LIABILITY 8.

In the present case, the accident has taken place on 01.04.2014, respondent No.2/Insurance Company is denying the liability on the reason that respondent No.1/owner has obtained permit from 07.05.2014 to 06.05.2019.
Ex.R-1 is permit, which proves that the permit to the vehicle was taken from 07.05.2014 to 06.05.2019.
The accident has caused on 01.04.2014, therefore, as on the date of accident there was no permit to the Auto Rickshaw.
Ex .R-4 is the driving licence, which proves that the driver of Auto Rickshaw was having driving licence to drive the light vehicle.
Insurance NC: 2024:KHC:45372 Policy was in existence as per Exs.R-2 and R-3, but it is proved that as on the date of accident there was no permit from the competent authorities.
Hence, respondent No.2/Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
But the owner of Auto Rickshaw is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, the Insurance Company is correctly exonerated.
Accordingly, the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence on record.
REGARDING PAY AND RECOVERY:
9. In the present case, the Tribunal has observed that the rider of the Auto Rickshaw had not possessed permit at the time of accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in exonerating the respondent No.2/Insurance Company from paying compensation to the appellant/claimant.

However, considering the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of PAPPU AND OTHERS Vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER1; NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. SWARAN SINGH AND OTHERS 2 and also as per the Full Bench decision of this Court in the case of NEW INDIA (2018) 3 SCC 208 (2 00 4 ) 3 SC C 297 NC:
2024:KHC:45372 ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. YELLAVVA AND ANOTHER3.

Therefore,
as per sub Sections (1) and (2) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act, an order of pay and recovery is made.
Hence, respondent No.2/Insurance Company is directed to pay compensation at first instance and then recover it from respondent No.1/owner of Auto Rickshaw as per law.

10. During recovery process, respondent No.2/Insurance Company is given liberty to file execution petition directly before concerned Jurisdictional Court and may seek attachment of movable or immovable properties till recovery of amount from respondent No.1/owner of offending vehicle.
Accordingly, an order of pay and recovery is made.

Therefore,

iv. No order as to costs.
v. The appellant/claimant is not entitled interest for the delayed period of 05 days in filing the appeal.
